PROCEDURE CODE
Art 1224
If it emerges either from an agreement of all the parties or from the opinion of the liquidating notary based, where applicable, on the report filed by the expert, that it is impossible to divide the property conveniently in kind, the liquidating notary draws up, unless all the parties agree to the sale by mutual agreement in accordance with article 1214, ¤ 1, paragraph 2, the specifications for the public sale of immovable property that cannot be conveniently divided in kind and summons the parties by bailiff's writ, by registered letter or against dated acknowledgement of receipt, as well as their advisers by ordinary mail, fax or electronic mail, to acquaint themselves with them and to inform him, in writing, of their objections within one month of the summons, unless all the parties agree otherwise as to this time limit. The summons must explicitly mention this time limit. At the same time, the liquidating notary summons the parties to follow up the sale.
In the absence of objections formulated by the parties in accordance with paragraph 1 on the principle of the sale, the liquidating notary is presumed to be required to continue the sale operations.
The auction is carried out at the request of at least one of the parties.
In the event of objections made by the parties in accordance with ¤ 1, either as to the principle of the sale or as to the conditions thereof, the liquidating notary acts in accordance with Article 1216.
if the court finds that convenient partition in kind is impossible, it orders the sale and sets, if applicable, a new time limit for the auction.
If the parties or the occupier of the immovable property whose sale is ordered are absent or fail to cooperate, the liquidating notary is authorised, at the expense of the general body of creditors, to gain access to the immovable property concerned, if necessary with the assistance of the police, assisted, if necessary, by a locksmith, in order to ensure compliance with the conditions of sale or to allow interested persons to visit the premises.
The occupier shall be informed of the judgement and of the days and times of the visit stipulated in the conditions of sale.
If the failure to cooperate is due to the occupier of the property ordered to be sold, the estate, where applicable represented by the manager referred to in article 1212, is entitled to recover its costs and any damages from the occupier. If the occupier is one of the undivided co-owners and no manager referred to in article 1212 has yet been appointed, such a manager shall be appointed at the request of the most diligent party to act to this end; in this case, the costs shall be recovered on behalf of the other undivided co-owners.
Paragraphs 2 to 4 are repeated in the judgment ordering the sale of the immovables.
If requested by at least one of the parties, the notary-liquidator proceeds with the sale of the immovables in accordance with what is customary for ordinary public sales of immovables and in accordance with article 1193, paragraphs 2 to 8, and, where applicable, in accordance with articles 1186 to 1192.
The notary-liquidator summons the parties, by bailiff's writ, by registered letter or by dated acknowledgement of receipt, to attend the sale and informs their counsel by ordinary mail, fax or e-mail.
The auction is carried out at the request of at least one of the parties.
 After the sale, the proceedings continue in accordance with article 1223.
 If the court finds that convenient partition in kind is possible, its judgment has, for the purposes of Article 1218, ¤ 3, 3¡, the effects of the judgment given in application of Article 1216.
If, due to the location of the immovables, several separate valuations have been carried out and if each immovable has been declared not conveniently divisible in kind, there is no need for an auction if it results from the comparison of the reports that all of the immovables can be conveniently divided.
In this case, the notary-liquidator divides the property and acts as provided for in Article 1223.
